assign.outcome: **Recommend 1-5 rubric levels over a topic-scoped, derived reputation log, with founder-owns/owner-overrides governance and zero voting in the MVP.** Levels are a display band recomputed live from reputation (cheap to relabel later); reputation follows `notes/auth/readme.md` §5's derived-points pattern (append-only action log, `SUM(weight)` per topic, one action per user per item enforced by a DB constraint) and gates exactly one privilege at launch — subtopic suggestion. Governance: topic founder owns by default, platform owner can override anything, every override logged the same as a mod action; no community voting anywhere in the MVP (no quorum at MVP scale). The §33 record is on the **reputation formula**, not the level scale — the scale is a relabel, the formula rewrites everyone's history if changed. Prior art dug in full with published rules linked: Stack Overflow privileges + its post-ChatGPT collapse, Reddit karma + the 2023 mod revolt (7,800+ subreddits), Wikipedia governance (RfA/ArbCom/deletionism) + its editor decline, Discord's positional role hierarchy, Duolingo streaks/retention + dark-pattern criticism, Khan Academy's Mastery-vs-Energy-Points split, university 100/200/300 numbering, freeCodeCamp/Codecademy's labour-market signal, Scouts' multi-gate Eagle ladder, martial-arts McDojo belt-inflation, and two 2023-24 gamification meta-analyses (g≈0.78-0.82, collapsing 5× for interventions past a few weeks). Every Challenge-section hypothesis was attacked directly (academic numbering, levels-on-every-topic, single reputation number, MVP voting, gamification evidence) and rejected or narrowed with reasons in the log.
